name: finals-2016-game7
title: Overtime Desk | 2016 NBA Finals Game 7: Cleveland 93, Golden State 89
description: Frozen historical fixture for the offline proof of the show: the final score, the block and the three from Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals, with sources.
notes: Play diagrams are original recreations drawn from the public play-by-play. No game footage, stills or audio are used. Facts are frozen as of the sources' box score and play-by-play pages.

segments.headline: Cavaliers 93, Warriors 89: Cleveland finishes the comeback from 3–1 down
segments.narration: Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals, June 19 at Oracle Arena in Oakland. The Cavaliers beat the Warriors 93 to 89 and became the first team to win the Finals after trailing three games to one. LeBron James finished with 27 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists. Kyrie Irving scored 26. Draymond Green led Golden State with 32 points, 15 rebounds and 9 assists.

claims.text: First team to win the Finals after trailing 3–1

segments.headline: The block: tied at 89 with 1:50 to play
segments.narration: Tied at 89 with under two minutes left, Golden State ran a two-on-one break. Andre Iguodala took the return pass from Stephen Curry and went up for the layup. LeBron James came from behind and pinned the ball on the glass with one minute fifty to play. Neither team had scored in more than two and a half minutes, and the game stayed tied.

segments.headline: Kyrie's step-back over Curry: 92–89 with 53 seconds left
segments.narration: With 53 seconds left and the score still 89 all, Kyrie Irving isolated against Stephen Curry on the right wing. He stepped back behind the arc and made the three for a 92 to 89 lead. Kevin Love then stayed in front of Curry on the next possession, and the three missed. LeBron James split two free throws with 10.6 seconds left for the final margin, 93 to 89.
